chapter: Second European tour and the crash
title: Ufa Palast, the rise of Hitler and a tour to Vienna
summary: After six weeks at the Ufa Palast and Hamburg, the band tours Spain, Italy and Vienna; he saw Nazi organizing already.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, when you came back to the Ufe Palace, you were already known in Berlin. You already had a following.

Oh yes. That's the reason they sent for us. They had this Ernie Rappe there, an American. Because things were down there, you know, in those days it wasn't so good either. Germany needed a shot in the arm. And they began to get it through the organization, that was looking Hitler, began raising his head, this dragon, you know. And you'd see them travelling with their packs on their backs and they'd meet -- the Nazi Party was being organized all the time, see. Which he caught me in time. Cause he caught me right after in '32.
So, how long were you at the Ufe Palace?
It was something like six weeks.

And then after that, we went to the Triechter in Hamburg, and we stayed there another four weeks. Then we made a tour all the way out to Turkey. And we played all the way along. We were seeing nothing but the casinos. Like the San Sebastien Casino in San Sebastien. Well, it was one of the places where the Spanish king stayed in the summertime. And then we played in Italy, in Milano and Florence and -- we didn't play Rome for some reason, we had to leave. I don't know what happened. And then we went back to Vienna and we played in a place called the Moulin Rouge in Vienna. And it was a funny thing there, we had a chance to go in St. Stephens Church there and go down in the catacombs and see, when John and Paul threw back the Arab squad, the Mohammedan bunch, a lot of the Turks were imprisoned and their skulls are down there like cans of tomatoes. Down in the catacombs. So we had a chance to visit that.
And we was well thought of in Vienna. In fact, we really loved Vienna.
